about: Requirements for a floor-mounted water closet: the fixture itself, its wall clearances and, in the ADA variant, grab bars and flush control. Read by the rhino-model skill's planner; each entry becomes one or more checks in the document's requirements once the layout is known.
status: Code values checked on 2026-11-04 against the text of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (ada.gov) and of IPC 405.3.1 as reproduced in IBC 2024 [P] 2903.1.1; product dimensions are defaults, not code. Use the project's adopted code and edition when the brief names one, and say which edition each value comes from.
local_code: These variants are US codes. For a project elsewhere, ask for the local code as a blocking question and never supply its values from memory. When none is available, a value from here is a stand-in: set the requirements' `code` to status stand-in, so every report says so.

frame.origin: finished floor, on the toilet centerline, at the face of the finished back wall
frame.x: along the back wall; the nearest side wall, when there is one, is on -x; the open (transfer) side is +x
frame.y: out from the back wall into the room
frame.use: Convert every value to world coordinates from the layout constants before writing checks. A toilet facing -y or with its side wall on +x mirrors the signs and swaps min and max.

symbols.P: projection: y of the front of the bowl (the Toilet extent max_y as built)
symbols.W: x of the side wall's finished face (negative)
symbols.B: z of the underside of the rear grab bar

layers.note: Child layers under the brief's parent. Checks find layers by keyword, so keep these words in the layer names, and keep them out of other elements' names: a layer named "Toilet paper dispenser" is counted as part of the toilet. Keep the seat lid off the Seat layer: seat height is measured to the top of the seat.

standard.use_when: the brief asks for a toilet, WC or bathroom without accessibility terms

requirements.what: Every toilet part is a closed, named solid
Bowl, seat, lid, tank and flush handle modeled
Top of seat 15-16 in above the finished floor (standard height)
requirements.source: default: standard-height two-piece toilet, manufacturer data

requirements.what: Front of bowl 28-31 in from the finished back wall (elongated bowl)
requirements.source: default: elongated two-piece toilet, manufacturer data

requirements.what: Overall width 17-22 in (the tank is the widest part)
Top of tank lid 27-31 in above the finished floor
Tank stands 0.25-2 in off the finished back wall
requirements.source: default: 12 in rough-in with a standard tank

requirements.what: Centerline 15 in min from any side wall, partition or obstruction
21 in min clear in front of the toilet to any wall, fixture or door
requirements.repeat_for: each other fixture or door layer in the model

requirements.what: Drain centered 12 in from the finished back wall (rough-in)
requirements.stated: rough-in 12 in: a placement constant; the drain is not modeled
requirements.source: default: standard rough-in (10 and 14 in also exist)

requirements.what: Flush handle on the tank front, left side facing the toilet
requirements.stated: flush handle side: typical product, not a requirement

ada.use_when: the brief says ADA, accessible, wheelchair, barrier-free or public; confirm the variant with the user when the brief is unclear

requirements.what: Top of seat 17-19 in above the finished floor
Centerline 16-18 in from the side wall or partition

Clearance 60 in min measured perpendicular from the side wall and 56 in min measured perpendicular from the rear wall, free of walls and other fixtures (the toilet, its grab bars and the room's own routes may overlap it)
requirements.repeat_for: each other fixture layer (lavatory, shower, door swing)

requirements.what: Side wall grab bar 42 in min long, starting 12 in max from the rear wall and extending 54 in min from it
Rear wall grab bar 36 in min long, extending 12 in min from the centerline toward the side wall and 24 in min toward the open side
Top of gripping surface 33-36 in above the finished floor, both bars
1.5 in between each grab bar and its wall
requirements.note: measure the gripping bar only; put mounting flanges on their own layer

requirements.what: Top of tank lid 27 in min above the floor and 1.5 in min below the rear grab bar
requirements.note: 1.5 in min to projecting objects below the bar (609.3). The 604.5.2 exceptions cover a recessed fixture beside the toilet and flush valves only; if the tank cannot clear the bar, ask before departing from the code.
requirements.source: default: two-piece toilet, manufacturer data; ADA 2010 609.3

requirements.what: Circular grab bars 1.25-2 in outside diameter
requirements.stated: grab bar diameter 1.25-2 in: set by the modeling constant

requirements.what: Grab bars and mounts resist 250 lbf
requirements.stated: grab bar strength 250 lbf: not modeled

requirements.what: Flush control on the open side of the water closet, operable part 15-48 in above the floor
Toilet paper dispenser 7-9 in in front of the water closet, measured to its centerline, outlet 15-48 in above the floor, not behind grab bars, and 1.5 in min below the grab bar above it
requirements.note: min_z takes the housing underside as the outlet; say so. B is the rear bar's underside; use the side bar's if it differs. Continuous paper flow (604.7) is a product specification: state it. 604.7 also says the dispenser shall not be located behind grab bars: never between the bar and the wall; below the bar with the 609.3 clearance is fine.

requirements.what: Seat not sprung to return to a lifted position

merge: When two entries constrain the same layer and key, use the intersection of their ranges and cite both sources; a variant's 'replaces' list names the base entries it supersedes.
